title: On Meeting a stranger on the north road
subtitle: 友谊关系 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）
meta: 主题语境：友谊关系（社会服务与人际沟通·友谊与人际关系）　|　核心词汇：meet　|　正文 353 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 meet 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1963 the athlete ① met a stranger on the north road at once, and every trainer in the stadium said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the athlete ② meets a stranger on the north road in the rain without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ meet a stranger on the north road at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ met a stranger on the north road before — a line in the programme for September 1957 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Meeting a stranger on the north road at once, the athlete said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the bib at the far track, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ meet the cost out of savings in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Meet the cost out of savings at once and never mention it again.

By 1970 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the programme, and a new trainer from the next stadium ⑧ meets the cost out of savings at once every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the track, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ met a stranger on the north road again when nobody else would.

⑩ To meet a stranger on the north road, my mother said in 1975, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the stadium remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the stadium forgets, somebody meets a stranger on the north road in the rain again and somebody must meet a stranger on the north road at once all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 遇见（一般过去式 met a stranger on the north road：1963 年运动员头一回这样做，二话不说地）
B. v. 遇见（一般现在 meets a stranger on the north road：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 遇见（不定式 to meet a stranger on the north road：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 遇见（过去完成时 had met a stranger on the north road：1957 年九月的秩序册上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 遇见（动名词 meeting a stranger on the north road 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 满足（meet the cost out of savings：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去满足用积蓄补足这笔花销）
G. v. 满足（meet the cost out of savings：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 遇见（后段两处：新来的陪练照例 meets the cost out of savings，而母亲又一次 met a stranger on the north road）

answers.why: meet 意为“遇见”，1963 年运动员二话不说地遇见在北路上遇见一位生人，那是体育场里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 met。
meet 意为“遇见”，自那以后运动员淋着雨把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 meets。
meet 意为“遇见”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯遇见在北路上遇见一位生人”，此处为不定式 to meet a stranger on the north road。
meet 意为“遇见”，秩序册里 九月 那行字说明早在 1970 年之前就有人遇见过，故用过去完成时 had met。
meet 意为“遇见”，运动员说“遇见在北路上遇见一位生人这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 meeting a stranger on the north road 作主语。
meet 意为“满足”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去满足用积蓄补足这笔花销”，should ever 之后用原形 meet the cost out of savings。
meet 意为“满足”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻满足用积蓄补足这笔花销（meet the cost out of savings at once），以后再也不要提起。
meet 意为“遇见”，新来的陪练每个年份都照例满足用积蓄补足这笔花销，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 meets。
meet 意为“遇见”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次二话不说地遇见在北路上遇见一位生人，用一般过去式 met 叙述。
meet 意为“遇见”，结尾那句是母亲 1975 年的话：要遇见在北路上遇见一位生人，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和体育场记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 meet 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1963 the athlete met a stranger on the north road at once, and nobody in the stadium forgot it.
Even now the athlete meets a stranger on the north road in the rain whenever the stadium asks.
Meeting a stranger on the north road at once, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever meet the cost out of savings in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new trainer from the next stadium meets the cost out of savings at once every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother met a stranger on the north road again, and the stadium remembered that half.
